extracted.intended_audience: Navy procurement and program managers (claimants, contracting officers, QAEs), OPNAV-443, installation managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for implementing the Department of the Navy's Commercial Activities (CA) program, including pre- and post-award practices, PWS formulation, contract administration, cost accounting, mobilization readiness, contract type selection, multifunction contracting, and training. Aimed at improving accuracy of cost comparisons and sustaining quality performance when functions are contracted out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for centralized claimant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for centralized guidance at the claimant level throughout the CA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement measures such as staffing CA Program implementation offices adequately (at least two people even at smaller claimancies), field CA implementation teams for on-site assistance at key milestones (writing the PWS, forming the MEO, conducting the cost comparison), publishing periodic 'Lessons Learned' synopses, and convening command meetings ~60-90 days prior to transition to highlight contract specifications and problem areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy (including contract administration and dealing with performance problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current instructions focus on pre-award process; there is a need for systematic direction on post-award issues including contract administration and handling contractor performance problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include claimants publishing a Quality Assurance Manual (sampling techniques, checklists, measurement issues), establishing QAE training or obtaining quotas, OPNAV-443 issuing an instruction on post-award conversion issues with contingency planning guidance, streamlining procedures for rapid government staffing and temporary contractor onboarding, and establishing a central contingency fund at OPNAV-443 to assist commands assembling contingency operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and clarity of Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The adequacy of performance is substantially determined by the clarity and completeness of the PWS; defining performance requirements is complex, especially for operations that change over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate sufficient resources to PWS preparation (consider funding additional resources during cost comparison), develop CA functional experts at the claimant level to assist in PWS formulation, improve availability/publicity of PWS preparation training, conduct audits/research on complex operations and multi-function contracts to evaluate PWS adequacy, and sequence CA reviews from simple to complex to build PWS expertise at activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of contract administration cost estimates and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons often underestimate post-award contract administration costs; actual contract administration costs routinely exceed the 4-8% estimates historically used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely monitor contract administration costs through better cost control/accounting systems, recognize that OMB staffing standards may be lower than field practice for contracts > $1M, negotiate QA staffing where possible, and consider that investment in contract administration appears to be a major factor in attaining/maintaining quality contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of cost accounting systems / 'cost yardsticks'
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing financial/accounting systems do not capture costs by CA function, making comparison of estimated and actual costs difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop better cost yardsticks that capture post-award costs by CA function (contract administration, litigation, contingency/performance costs, clerical support, training, morale impacts), and improve systems so managers can meaningfully compare estimated vs actual costs (adjusting for assumptions like prevailing wages, scope, periods of performance). Chapter V recommends implementing a control system to monitor contract administration and other post-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of standard cost factors (e.g., fringe benefits factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factors (averages) can distort cost estimates by inflating some operations and deflating others; the fringe benefits factor used in CA comparisons has been controversial and inconsistent with other Navy budgeting factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct research into rationale and differences between competing factors (e.g., 27.05% vs 16-17%), and be cautious using averages when costs vary widely across functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of contracting out on budget flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractual obligations reduce local commanders' budget flexibility during across-the-board budget cuts because contract funds are legally obligated and may prevent realistic distribution reflecting mission criticality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNO should provide general guidelines and alternatives for dealing with funding reductions for activities/claimants with large multi-function contracts; analyze budget flexibility impacts when deciding to contract out functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type selection (sealed bid/one-step vs negotiated/two-step)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether procurement is sealed bid (one-step) or negotiated (two-step) directly impacts quality of performance, especially in complex operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on data, negotiated procurement should be the only procurement type allowed for complex operations to allow flexibility and better technical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract pricing/award-fee structure effects on QA/documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Plus Award Fee contracts have less documentation attached to the award fee aspect (not subject to the Disputes Clause) and may provide more positive incentives and streamlined QA requirements compared with Firm Fixed Price contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct closer cost analyses comparing Firm Fixed Price and Cost Plus Award Fee approaches to determine differences in contract administration costs and quality of performance; consider potential QA/documentation tradeoffs when selecting contract type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-function (BOS) vs single-function contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-function or BOS contracts often achieve better and smoother operations, provide a single contractor focal point, and can yield economies of scale; they also provide a government focal point in the Service Contract Manager (SCM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider combining small single-function contracts into larger multifunction contracts to allow flexibility, better workforce and equipment utilization, simplified contract administration, single point-of-contact benefits, and easier handling of overlapping/ interdependent support functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilization readiness of contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: There is debate about contractor readiness under mobilization; some studies find mobilization readiness generally not a problem for low-skill housekeeping services, but uncertainty remains for larger critical support contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To minimize mobilization risk: have mobilization plans, delineate mobilization requirements in solicitations, include mobilization clauses in contracts, require contractors to plan for recall of former military personnel, and include contractors in mobilization planning and exercises where appropriate. Facilities with major contracts should take steps to ensure contractor readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency/resolution options for poor contractor performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities need options for dealing with poor contractor performance post-award, including forming contingency plans and quickly assembling temporary operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPNAV-443 should issue instruction outlining options, consider streamlining government personnel recruiting/detailing for rapid assembly, provide streamlined procedures for onboarding temporary contractors, and establish a central contingency fund to financially assist activities that must assemble contingency operations pending resolicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-level implementation assistance (on-site teams & milestone visits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field CA implementation teams should conduct on-site assistance at field activities undergoing the CA process at significant milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visits timed for writing the PWS, forming the MEO, conducting the cost comparison, etc., will allow activities to benefit from lessons learned elsewhere and develop real-life expertise at claimant level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination of lessons learned and command rosters
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing and distributing 'Lessons Learned' and an annual list of commands that have undergone CA reviews (sorted by functional area) helps activities find proven PWSs and learn from prior implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit regular inputs from activities, distribute widely within the claimancy, submit recaps to OPNAV-443 annually, and have major claimants disseminate the annual lists to commands scheduled for CA reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance (QA) program quality and manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-written and well-implemented QA programs reduce hidden costs and support quality contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants should publish a Quality Assurance Manual (how-to for QAEs) including sampling techniques, checklists, measurement issues; provide QAE training quotas/courses; improve QA sampling and measurement capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and training for contract administration and CA implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate staffing and limited expertise (including attrition) in CA implementation, contract administration, COTRs, QAEs, and contracting officers (KOs) reduces program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide more comprehensive, better publicized, and accessible training on CA program, PWS formulation, cost comparison process, and QA; consider special KO training on CA contractual options; expand course quotas and instructors with real-life CA experience; staff claimant implementation offices adequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: KO (Contracting Officer) expertise in CA procurements
rubrics_metrics.description: KOs may have gaps in knowledge of contractual options in CA procurements and their choices affect procurement type, contract type, and technical evaluation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide additional research and special training for KOs involved in CA procurements so they can choose the best contract vehicle and procurement method to obtain best value for the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizing review sequencing (simple-to-complex CA reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling CA reviews so that simpler CA functions are reviewed first and sequence moves to more complex functions helps build experience in PWS preparation and CA implementation at the base level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task base commanders to schedule reviews from simple to complex to allow expertise to evolve before tackling complex operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and controlling post-award events and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring of post-award events and costs in the CA program is loosely structured, which undermines objective assessment of program success and cost savings claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement formal post-award control systems and better cost accounting to maintain actual cost data in forms useful for program management; without these, assessments of program success/failure and cost savings are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tech/automation investment vs CA program ROI for complex operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex operations (storage/warehousing, multifunction contracts), investing in automation, improved computer technology, and robotics may yield a better return on investment than contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reallocating resources toward automation and efficiency programs for complex operations or financially assisting commands during PWS preparation if contracting out is chosen; re-evaluate inclusion of complex operations in the CA inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate true costs of contract administration under different contract forms
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be differences in contract administration costs and performance quality between Firm Fixed Price and Cost Plus Award Fee contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct analyses to determine the true cost of contract administration and any differences in performance quality under Firm Fixed Price versus Cost Plus Award Fee contracts to inform contract type selection.
